text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Danish opposition Conservative Party leader Hans Engell proposes that a national referendum be held in spring 1998 on the results of the inter-governmental conference on reforms to the European Union, coupled with Denmark's Maastricht Treaty opt-out on participating in joint refugee and police policy.

--- Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen says that it is up to Greenland to decide whether or not it wants to remain inside the Danish commonwealth or declare independence, stressing that Copenhagen has no intention of intervening in the current debate on the issue in its Arctic island province.

--- Several of Denmark's largest food companies, including Danisco and Toms Chocolates, are cooperating in a common export offensive in China with the aim of upping sales of Danish products in Chinese supermarkets.

--- Danish exports to new growth markets in eastern Europe, the Far East and Latin America have doubled to 45 billion crowns in the past six years and are expected to account for 30 percent of the country's total exports in the year 2005.
--- The number of Danes on public benefits fell at end-1996 for the first time in seven years by 21,000 to 938,000, about one fifth of the country's entire population.
